purpose: Reviewable open question and visible payoff variants for approved topics. Existing approved briefs remain the current content.

variants.opening: What are these white crystals inside your Parmigiano?
variants.openingVisual: Begin on a macro image with the crystals visible. Show a small piece breaking away with stable geometry.
variants.payoff: They are tyrosine crystals, formed as the cheese matures.
variants.payoffVisual: Reveal the same crystals in the cheese interior with a concise tyrosine caption.
sequence: Explain that maturation breaks down milk proteins.
Show the crystals and explain the release of amino acids.
Name tyrosine and connect it to the original close-up.
Finish with the existing viewer question.
variants.review: Keep useful explanation between question and answer. Check the appearance against a real cheese reference.
variants.originalOpening: Those white crystals in Parmigiano Reggiano are not salt.

sources.title: Parmigiano Reggiano Consortium FAQ
claims: The visible white crystals described in the FAQ are tyrosine, an amino acid.
Tyrosine is released as proteins break down during maturation.
The crystals become larger and more numerous with longer maturation.

variants.opening: What was inside this chocolate egg that sold for seven thousand pounds?
variants.openingVisual: Show a partially opened illustrative chocolate shell. Put 2012 charity auction on screen.
variants.payoff: The fillings included caramel, Japanese black vinegar, rosemary and olive oil.
variants.payoffVisual: Reveal an illustrative filling cutaway. Keep the AI illustration disclosure.
sequence: Ask the filling question with the historical date visible.
State London charity auction in 2012 and the fifty kilo weight.
Explain the three days of work by seven chocolatiers.
Finish with break it open or keep it untouched.
variants.review: Do not imply that the generated interior is documentary evidence of the actual auction egg.
variants.originalOpening: Seven thousand pounds for chocolate. This happened at a London charity auction in twenty twelve.

sources.title: Guinness World Records report, 21 March 2012
claims: A 50 kilogram chocolate egg sold for £7,000 at a London charity auction in March 2012.
It was designed by William Curley.
Seven chocolatiers worked for three days.
Fillings included muscovado caramel, Japanese black vinegar, rosemary and olive oil.
The report described a non-jewelled chocolate egg record in 2012, not a current record.

variants.opening: How did saffron help pay for these Italian towers?
variants.openingVisual: Connect visible saffron threads with an illustrative view of San Gimignano. Avoid fabricated historical imagery presented as evidence.
variants.payoff: Some families used profits from the saffron trade to help finance their towers.
variants.payoffVisual: Return to the skyline when the financing explanation lands.
sequence: Identify San Gimignano and the documented medieval saffron trade.
Resolve the financing question with the limited some families claim.
Finish with the existing towers or saffron choice.
variants.review: Keep helped finance and some families. Avoid implying saffron alone built the skyline.
variants.originalOpening: A spice helped pay for the towers of an Italian town.

sources.title: Visit Tuscany official tourism: PDO San Gimignano saffron
claims: Saffron trade profits helped some families finance San Gimignano towers.
Trade is documented from the thirteenth century.
The PDO production area is the territory of San Gimignano.
Flower picking, separating stigmas and drying still involve manual work.
